purpose: Calcifediol is used to treat secondary hyperparathyroidism, which means your parathyroid glands are working too hard because your body is low on active vitamin D. It is mainly prescribed for adults who have chronic kidney disease and are not on dialysis. Keeping your vitamin D levels in a healthy range helps protect your bones and keeps certain hormones in balance.
how_it_works: Your liver naturally converts vitamin D into calcifediol, which is a storage form of vitamin D in your body. When you take this medication, it raises the level of calcifediol in your blood, giving your kidneys more material to work with to make the active form of vitamin D your body needs. This helps calm down the overactive parathyroid glands and keeps calcium and phosphorus levels more balanced.
common_side_effects: Anemia (low red blood cell count), high levels of calcium or phosphorus in the blood, swelling in the legs or ankles, constipation, runny nose, cough, and shortness of breath. Some people may also notice increased thirst or urination.
warnings: If you take too much, calcium can build up to dangerously high levels in your blood — a condition called hypercalcemia. This can cause serious heart and kidney problems. Tell your doctor right away if you feel very thirsty, urinate a lot, feel confused, or have nausea and vomiting. Avoid taking extra vitamin D or calcium supplements unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Your doctor will regularly check your blood levels while you are on this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 30 micrograms taken by mouth once daily at bedtime. Your doctor may increase the dose to 60 micrograms once daily after about 3 months if your blood levels are not where they need to be. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
